## REQ-IL-001

**Every asset is identified by an Identification Link**

Every asset (application or device) represented on the Message Bus is identified by exactly one Identification Link (IL string according to IEC 61406-1).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Refs: MG 4, MG 4.1
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4-7bcaa186, MG-4.1-02958e7d

> Every asset (device or application) that is represented on the Message Bus must be identified by an Identification Link.
> — MG 4

## REQ-IL-002

**Identification Link in topics is base64url-encoded**

In the topic elements AppId and Source, the Identification Link is encoded as follows: its UTF-8 octets are encoded with base64url (RFC 4648, section 5), the padding characters "=" are omitted and no line breaks or other characters are added. The result forms exactly one topic level.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 4, MG 4.2
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4-30944928, MG-4.2-1b9c4809

> In the topic, the Identification Link must always be base64url-encoded and must form exactly one topic level
> — MG 4

> Whenever an Identification Link is used as a topic element (AppId, see 7.3 AppId Element, and Source, see 7.6 Source Element), it must be encoded as follows
> — MG 4.2

> The padding characters = are omitted
> — MG 4.2

Notes: Topic grammar rule encoded-il (topic/topic.abnf); vectors V-IL-1xx and V-TOP-….

## REQ-IL-003

**Standard Base64 alphabet is not used in topics**

The encoded Identification Link in a topic does not use the standard Base64 alphabet (RFC 4648, section 4): it contains no "+" and no "/".

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 4.2
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.2-25d30dc8, MG-4.2-6a558e64

> The standard Base64 alphabet (RFC 4648, section 4) must not be used, because it contains the characters + and /, which have a special meaning in MQTT topics.
> — MG 4.2

## REQ-IL-004

**Exactly one valid encoded representation**

A topic element AppId or Source is a valid encoded Identification Link only if it is the canonical base64url encoding without padding of a valid Identification Link: it contains only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, "-" and "_", its length is not 1 modulo 4, the unused bits of its last character are zero, and the decoded string fulfills the constraints of MG 4.1 (REQ-IL-016, REQ-IL-018, REQ-IL-019). Any other topic element is invalid.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 4.2
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.2-213ad616

> Therefore, there must be exactly one valid encoded representation for each Identification Link.
> — MG 4.2

> A topic element that contains padding characters = or any character outside the base64url alphabet is not a valid encoded Identification Link.
> — MG 4.2

Notes: "Canonical" (zero padding bits) follows from "exactly one valid encoded representation": a non-canonical last character decodes to the same octets with lenient decoders. Grammar rules b64-tail2/b64-tail3; the maximum length of 340 characters follows from REQ-IL-019.

## REQ-IL-008

**Identification Link fulfills IEC 61406-1**

An Identification Link (including an Oi4Identifier) fulfills all requirements of IEC 61406-1 and the constraints of MG 4.1.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, manufacturer
- Refs: MG 4.1, MG 4.3.2
- Verification: d7-validate, manual

> An Identification Link used in an Open Industry 4.0 Alliance system must fulfill all requirements of IEC 61406-1.
> — MG 4.1

> It must meet all the requirements outlined in that specification and in 4.1 IEC 61406-1 Identification Link, as well as the requirements specified in this document.
> — MG 4.3.2

Notes: D7 checks the testable constraints (REQ-IL-009, REQ-IL-016, REQ-IL-018, REQ-IL-019); the prohibited character combinations with special functions of IEC 61406-1 cannot be checked (MG 4.1) and stay with the issuer.

## REQ-IL-009

**Components of an Identification Link**

An Identification Link has the form "[&lt;scheme>://]&lt;authority>[/&lt;path>][?&lt;query>][#&lt;fragment>]" (URL syntax according to RFC 3986). The authority is mandatory and non-empty; it is the internet domain of the issuer, which is under the control of the issuer. Scheme, path, query and fragment are optional.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, manufacturer
- Refs: MG 4.1
- Verification: d7-validate, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.1-29fce8a3, MG-4.1-440b8efa, MG-4.1-6c978eac, MG-4.1-cb8c52f1

> The domain must be under the control of the issuer of the Identification Link (typically the manufacturer).
> — MG 4.1

Notes: D7 checks a non-empty authority (the part after an optional "&lt;scheme>://" up to the first "/", "?" or "#"); the control of the domain is checked manually.

## REQ-IL-013

**Identification Link is used exactly as assigned**

An Identification Link is used exactly as assigned by the issuer: it is not altered, completed or normalized – no scheme is added or removed, the case of characters is not changed and no characters are (percent-)encoded or decoded.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 4.1
- Verification: d7-test, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.1-4ec656cf, MG-4.1-59c67bae, MG-4.1-85a3434f, MG-4.1-b797c8d0, MG-4.1-bbfe604c

> An Identification Link must be used exactly as it was assigned by the issuer.
> — MG 4.1

> It must not be altered, completed or normalized in any way.
> — MG 4.1

Notes: D7 compares the decoded AppId/Source with the ProductInstanceUri of the MAM and the identifiers in the payload character by character.

## REQ-IL-015

**Identification Links are compared character by character**

Two Identification Links are equal if and only if they are equal character by character (case-sensitive); no RFC 3986 normalization is applied. In particular, an Identification Link with scheme and the same Identification Link without scheme are different Identification Links.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: component
- Refs: MG 4.1
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.1-54cd2342, MG-4.1-760625d5

> An Identification Link with scheme and the same Identification Link without scheme shall be treated as different Identification Links.
> — MG 4.1

> Two Identification Links are equal if and only if they are equal character by character (case-sensitive).
> — MG 4.1

## REQ-IL-016

**Allowed characters of an Identification Link**

An Identification Link contains only the ASCII characters permitted by IEC 61406-1 (Annex A): letters, digits, "-", ".", "_", "~" and the reserved characters ":", "/", "?", "#", "[", "]", "@", "!", "$", "&", "'", "(", ")", "*", "+", ",", ";", "=" (according to their function in the URL syntax). Space, '"', "%", "&lt;", ">", "\", "^", "`", "{", "|", "}", control characters and non-ASCII characters are not permitted.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, manufacturer
- Refs: MG 4.1
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.1-67568a97, MG-4.1-771b37b4

> Only the ASCII characters permitted by IEC 61406-1 (Annex A) may be used.
> — MG 4.1

> The following characters are not permitted: space, ", %, &lt;, >, \, ^, , {, |, }, control characters and all non-ASCII characters.
> — MG 4.1

Notes: "Only … may be used" restricts the character set; recorded as MUST. Whether a reserved character is used according to its URL function cannot be checked in general (IEC 61406-1); D7 checks the character set.

## REQ-IL-017

**Values with special characters are masked**

If a value used in the path, query or fragment of an Identification Link (e.g. a serial number) contains characters that are not permitted or have a special function in the URL syntax, they are masked by other means than percent-encoding, e.g. by the dnp-encoding (MG A3).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, manufacturer
- Refs: MG 4.1, MG A3
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.1-2565d666, MG-A3-bb77d6ad

> If values (e.g. a serial number) contain characters that are not permitted or have a special function in the URL syntax, they must be masked by other means.
> — MG 4.1

> In case one of the reserved or prohibited characters is part of the path, query or fragment, the character must be masked out to become a machine-readable URI again.
> — MG A3

**Authority in lowercase**

The authority (domain) of an Identification Link is written in lowercase characters. Path, query and fragment are case-sensitive and may contain uppercase characters.

## REQ-IL-021

**Filtering by parts of the Identification Link is done by the application**

A subscriber that needs assets of a specific manufacturer, model, product code or serial number subscribes to a specific encoded Identification Link or uses the single-level wildcard "+" and filters the received messages itself (e.g. based on the Master Asset Model); it does not rely on parts of the encoded topic element.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber
- Refs: MG 4.2
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.2-8195fcdf

> Filtering by manufacturer, model, product code or serial number must be done by the application, e.g. based on the Master Asset Model (5 The Master Asset Model).
> — MG 4.2

## REQ-IL-022

**Structure of the Oi4Identifier**

An Oi4Identifier has the form "&lt;ManufacturerUri>/&lt;Model>/&lt;ProductCode>/&lt;SerialNumber>" without scheme; all four elements are mandatory strings. The result is an Identification Link, so all its rules apply (REQ-IL-008, REQ-IL-016); characters that are not permitted, have a special function in the URL syntax or are a "/" inside an element are masked with the dnp-encoding (REQ-IL-017, REQ-IL-033).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application generates an Oi4Identifier.
- Refs: MG 4.3.1
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.3.1-1f4d5d6c, MG-4.3.1-8b0a5dee, MG-4.3.1-b4192d78

> The Oi4Identifier in the form of &lt;ManufacturerUri/Model/ProductCode/SerialNumber> represents an IEC 61406-1 compliant Identification Link (4.1 IEC 61406-1 Identification Link) without scheme.
> — MG 4.3.1

Notes: Reference implementation il.Oi4Identifier; vectors V-OID-…. Statement changed in C-046 addendum 2 (SF-104, PO 2026-10-26: MG 4.1 governs, the masking is mandatory): "may be masked" → "are masked".

## REQ-IL-024

**Form of the ManufacturerUri**

The ManufacturerUri is a lowercase internet domain name without scheme, port, path and without a leading "www.", typically of the form "&lt;manufacturer>.&lt;tld>"; a subdomain of the manufacturer's domain (e.g. id.provider.com) may be used.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application generates an Oi4Identifier.
- Refs: MG 4.3.1, SF-043
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.3.1-337aee99, MG-4.3.1-3ffb82de, MG-4.3.1-ee306191

> The ManufacturerUri must be the domain part of the manufacturer URL in lower case, where the scheme (e. g. https://), port and path as well as the third level domain, e.g. &lt;www> are excluded.
> — MG 4.3.1

> Typically, it is of the form &lt;manufacturer>.&lt;tld>; other subdomains may be used (see note below).
> — MG 4.3.1

> A manufacturer may use subdomains of its internet domain for use as ManufacturerUri if it is considered necessary.
> — MG 4.3.1

Notes: PO decision SF-043 (c) (C-020); reference check il.CheckManufacturerURI.

## REQ-IL-027

**Oi4Identifier elements from the Master Asset Model**

If the Master Asset Model of the identified asset contains the property Model, ProductCode or SerialNumber when the Oi4Identifier is generated, that value is used for the related element; for the LocalizedText Model the Text in the locale en-US is used, independent of a requested Locale.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application generates an Oi4Identifier.
- Refs: MG 4.3.1, MG 5, SF-064

**Oi4Identifier is known or retrievable**

An implementation that uses an Oi4Identifier ensures that it is known to all involved systems or can be easily retrieved, and that its elements identify the asset unambiguously.

## REQ-IL-032

**dnp-encoding**

The dnp-encoding keeps the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, "-", ".", "_" and "~" and writes every other octet of the UTF-8 representation as "," followed by two uppercase hexadecimal digits (e.g. space → ",20", "/" → ",2F", "," → ",2C", "ä" → ",C3,A4").

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application dnp-encodes a value (an Oi4Identifier element, REQ-IL-033).
- Refs: MG A3, SF-043
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-A3-d9344f53, MG-A3-ffe5198a

> A comma-encoding mechanism is used to represent a data octet in a component when that octet's corresponding character is outside the allowed set or is being used as a delimiter of, or within, the component.
> — MG A3

> This also applies to control characters and to all characters outside US-ASCII, which must not be used in an Identification Link either (e.g. the tabulator becomes ,09, the character ä with the UTF-8 octets C3 A4 becomes ,C3,A4).
> — MG A3

Notes: Defines how the encoding works; when it is used is REQ-IL-033 (MUST since SF-104, C-046 addendum 2; before MAY, SF-043 (e), C-019). Table 18 of MG A3 is the ASCII excerpt of the general rule for all UTF-8 octets (PO decision SF-043 (a), (b), C-020). Reference implementation il.DnpEncode; vectors V-DNP-….

## REQ-IL-033

**Oi4Identifier elements are dnp-encoded**

The generator of an Oi4Identifier writes Model, ProductCode and SerialNumber dnp-encoded (REQ-IL-032). Values made only of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, "-", ".", "_" and "~" stay unchanged; every other character is not permitted in an Identification Link, has a special function in the URL syntax (REQ-IL-017) or is the "/" that separates the elements, and is masked. So each nameplate gives exactly one Oi4Identifier (MG 4.3), and every "," in an element is a mask sign. The dnp-encoding is not used anywhere else; in topics the Identification Link is base64url-encoded (REQ-IL-002), and receivers do not decode it (REQ-IL-029).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application generates an Oi4Identifier.
- Refs: MG 4.3.1, MG A3, MG 4.1, SF-043, SF-104
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-4.3.1-8757ccac

> All requirements of IEC 61406-1 and 4.1 IEC 61406-1 Identification Link also apply to the Oi4Identifier.
> — MG 4.3.1

> If values (e.g. a serial number) contain characters that are not permitted or have a special function in the URL syntax, they must be masked by other means.
> — MG 4.1

> If a value of Model, ProductCode or SerialNumber contains other characters than A–Z, a–z, 0–9, -, ., _ and ~, the value must be dnp-encoded (A3 The dnp-Encoding), so that the Oi4Identifier can be regenerated from the same values.
> — MG 4.3.1

> In this case, these components are dnp-encoded (see 4.3.1 Structure of the Oi4Identifier).
> — MG A3

Notes: Changed in C-046 addendum 2 from MAY to MUST: PO decision SF-104 (2026-10-26) – MG 4.1 governs ("must be masked by other means"), the "may" of MG 4.3.1 and MG A3 names the means (dnp-encoding), not an option to leave such characters unmasked; masking only the offending characters equals encoding the whole element, because the dnp-encoding keeps exactly the unreserved characters. Guideline text of MG 4.3.1 and MG A3 aligned on PO order (C-046 review D-1, guideline 734c560; quotes and inventory remapped, the two former MAY sentences of MG A3 have no keyword any more). Before: PO decision SF-043 (e) (C-019, guideline 7de6cb8). Reference implementation il.Oi4Identifier applies the dnp-encoding; vectors V-OID-…; D7 checks it heuristically in the MAM (REQ-RES-MAM-006, V-PAY-245).

## REQ-IL-034

The ManufacturerUri corresponds to the domain of the Identification Link of the asset. In case of doubt, it is given without scheme and without third level domain ("&lt;manufacturer>.&lt;tld>").

- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD

- Status: reviewed

> — MG 4.3.1
